title: Face Skin Imaging System with AI Skin Analysis
summary: Learn how face and skin imaging can support beauty product discovery, virtual try-on, consultations, and conversion measurement across digital and in-store journeys.
body_markdown:
### What is face imaging in beauty?


Face imaging uses a customer-provided photo or camera input to support beauty discovery, consultation, and virtual experiences. Depending on the use case, it may help organize visible facial attributes, tones, proportions, or skin-related information into a more relevant customer journey.


### How can face imaging support conversion?


Face imaging can support conversion when it helps customers move from uncertainty to a useful next action, such as trying a look, comparing products, exploring a routine, or booking a consultation. Results should be measured against a defined business baseline rather than assumed.


### What should brands measure after launching face imaging?


Brands can measure adoption of the experience, product-detail views, add-to-cart behavior, checkout progression, conversion, consultation bookings, return reasons, and customer feedback. The right metric depends on the customer problem the experience is designed to solve.


### What is the difference between face imaging and a skin analyzer?


Face imaging can refer broadly to image-based beauty experiences involving facial attributes or visible skin information. A face checker generally focuses on facial features and proportions, while a skin analyzer focuses on visible skin concerns. Read our[face checker vs. skin analyzer guide](https://www.perfectcorp.com/business/blog/general/face-checker-analysis) for a fuller comparison.


### Is face imaging a medical diagnostic tool?


No. Beauty-oriented face and skin imaging can support cosmetic discovery and consultation but should not be presented as a medical diagnosis, treatment recommendation, or substitute for care from a qualified healthcare professional.
